messages:
maya: Heads-up — our int8 canary (raven-lite q4a) shows higher funcall parse failures on streaming requests vs non-streaming. raw parse fail rate +1.9% in canary window.
oliver: hmm, is this p95 latency or token truncation? any logs?
sam: looks like truncation. When we hit rate-cap autoscaler bursts, the stream cuts in the middle of the JSON array suffix. example from logs:
```
...\"actions\":[{\"name\":\"lookup\",\"args\":{...}},
<STREAM_CUTOFF>
```
so downstream parser gets an incomplete JSON object
maya: exact. non-streaming/gRPC path unaffected. suggests a batching/ratecap interaction in the streaming aggregator
sophia: interesting — could be continuous-batching flush boundary aligning with rate limiter. we saw similar with kv-prefix earlier but not exactly this pattern
oliver: can we reproduce locally with stress script? i'll try varying rate_cap_ms and batch_max_tokens
sam: repro steps I used:
```
rcli canary run --model raven-lite-q4a --mode streaming --qps 30 --duration 10m --payload ./samples/fncall-heavy.json
rcli metrics slice --canary run123 --metric funcall_parse_fail
```
maya: thanks. initial quick patch idea: append a deterministic terminator token in the prompt post-template like `<JSON_TERMINATOR>` and postprocess to strip it before parsing. low risk for canary
sophia: would prefer runtime fix: tweak streaming flush to ensure we flush on potential funcall suffix boundaries (detect `]}` or `\"})` patterns) — cheaper if we can pattern-match
oliver: both sound reasonable. sentinel is fastest to test. runtime change needs perf bench
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/prodstream-flush-probe v0.1 -> canary cluster (ami-2026-03-21)
sam: quick sentinel patch diff:
```
prompt = prompt + "\\n<JSON_TERMINATOR>"
// on client parse: strip everything after first occurrence of <JSON_TERMINATOR>
```
maya: ran sentinel canary for 20k requests — parse fail rate dropped from 3.2% -> 0.6%, but we introduced ~0.8% extra tokens per response (cost delta)
oliver: cost hit ok if reliability improved. need to check downstream tool invocation semantics — any risk tool sees the sentinel? we strip before funcall invocation right?
sophia: also let's try a second experiment: reduce batch_max_tokens by 20% when streaming funcall-enabled routes. that should reduce mid-object flushes without sentinel cost
maya: agreement: run two parallel canaries — sentinel vs reduced-batch. collect: funcall_parse_fail, p99-tail-token-loss, token_delta, cpu_alloc
sam: I'll kick them off and share results in ~45m
oliver: if sentinel wins but cost unacceptable, follow-up runtime change (smart flush) is next. :thumbsup:
maya: thanks all — adding a short note to the canary playbook and flagging for next eng-ml retro
sophia: saved logs to s3://redwood-canaries/6132123456/ — link: https://s3.redwood.internal/canaries/6132123456
deploy-bot: canary finished: run123 -> 45m, status: completed
sam: results posted: s3://redwood-canaries/6132123456/results.json
maya: quick summary in thread: sentinel reduced parse failures but raised token cost; reduced-batch reduced both failures and cost somewhat. next step: schedule small runtime flush patch and perf bench
oliver: ok filing follow-up ticket in phab: T12345
sophia: also add a monitor that alerts on sudden funcall parse delta >0.5% over baseline
maya: noted. :white_check_mark:
